claims.statement: Poland's Clean Air programme requires an energy audit and a programme-format audit summary, and the works must match the audit; this creates a recurring document-consistency gate rather than a discretionary productivity problem.

The official programme publishes structured forms and instructions for applications, audits, advance payments, contractor acceptance, and payment requests, which should make a rules-driven precheck technically feasible without automating the government's final decision.

Hypothesis: a heat-pump, insulation, or photovoltaic wholesaler can distribute the tool to hundreds of downstream installers because fewer rejected or delayed files improve both installer cash conversion and the wholesaler's sell-through.

contrary_evidence: The programme already provides a government application generator, manuals, templates, and municipal operator support, so a generic form filler would have little pricing power.
Programme rules changed again in July 2026, demonstrating that maintenance costs and rule-change risk are real.

economics.acquisition_route: One wholesaler, audit network, or municipal software partner can activate many installers; use the family installer only as a validation site
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 1500 active installers averaging 1000 PLN monthly plus channel fees could reach roughly 2.0-2.5 million PLN ARR in years 4-5; at 30% EBITDA, a 6-8x EBITDA value and at least 80% founder ownership could place founder equity above 5 million PLN in years 5-7, without double-counting retained cash
economics.founder_time: Initial 15-22 hours weekly for rules, parsing, and one integration; target under 8 hours weekly after partner onboarding and contracted domain review
economics.gross_margin_basis: Rules engine, document parsing, and support should support 75-88% software gross margin after model inference and partner support
economics.payback: Target partner acquisition payback under 6 months and installer payback from avoiding one material rework or delayed-payment episode
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 80-180 PLN per completed dossier or 900-1800 PLN per installer per month, plus 20000-60000 PLN annual white-label partner licence
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every subsidised job creates a repeat validation event; rule history and stored equipment evidence create workflow retention

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A versioned rule graph plus anonymised validation-error and equipment-document corpus improves checks and partner switching costs
fingerprint.customer: Polish retrofit installers, energy auditors, municipal programme operators, and their equipment wholesalers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embedded in wholesaler quoting portals, auditor software, and municipal operator workflows; resold to downstream installers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: White-label SaaS and API that validates audit-to-quote-to-acceptance evidence, sold per project plus channel licence
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Installer or channel partner pays per validated project file or per active installer seat when a dossier reaches payment-ready status
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A subsidised retrofit quote, audit, acceptance protocol, or payment request must be internally consistent before submission

founder_fit: Strong fit with the founder's renewable-energy family channel, Polish context, automation skills, and preference for a measurable product. A pilot can use synthetic files and consenting family-company cases while remaining part-time and avoiding public-facing selling.
risks: Incorrect eligibility advice could create financial and reputational liability; the product must remain a precheck with human sign-off.
A programme redesign or direct government validation feature could erase the wedge.
Installers may be fragmented and price-sensitive unless a channel partner subsidises adoption.

structure.control_point: The final internal approval gate before a contractor signs or submits a payment dossier
structure.critical_dependency: Continued partner access to real project documents and rapid maintenance against official programme rule changes

thesis: Build a white-label document-consistency and payment-readiness rail for Polish energy auditors, retrofit installers, and municipal Clean Air operators. The software would turn an audit and quote into a controlled checklist, equipment-evidence pack, acceptance protocol, and payment-file precheck, sitting inside the partner's existing quote-to-cash workflow rather than relying on direct homeowner acquisition.
title: Retrofit Proofrail
uncertainties: Actual rejection and rework rates by installer and document type are not public.
It is unproven whether wholesalers, auditors, or municipal operators have the strongest budget and integration incentive.
Government-system export and attachment formats may constrain a clean end-to-end workflow.
